topStories.headline: SF Opera Strike Ends: Tentative Four-Year Deal Clears the Way for Season to Open Sept. 22
topStories.dek: After a six-day walkout that canceled five performances, management and musicians reached a tentative agreement on Sept. 17, pending ratification by the full orchestra.
topStories.body:
The curtain at the War Memorial Opera House is finally set to rise on the 2026–27 season. <cite index="29-3,29-4">Five days after the San Francisco Opera Orchestra struck the season-opening performance of Verdi's Simon Boccanegra, the labor action came to an end when SF Opera and the orchestra, represented by the American Federation of Musicians Local 6, jointly announced they had reached a tentative settlement on a new four-year contract.</cite>

<cite index="29-5">The contract, which must still be ratified by orchestra members in a vote, would run retroactively from Aug. 1, 2026 through July 31, 2030.</cite> <cite index="34-5">Pending ratification, performances are set to resume when Verdi's Simon Boccanegra opens on Tuesday, Sept. 22.</cite>

<cite index="34-8,34-9,34-10">The San Francisco Opera Orchestra, represented by American Federation of Musicians Local 6, had been on strike since Sept. 12, when the season opener of Simon Boccanegra was canceled just a half hour before curtain. In the days since, a picket line and impromptu performances took place intermittently on the Opera House steps. Musicians also performed casually in Golden Gate Park on Sunday, Sept. 13, while technicians dismantled the stage for Opera in the Park, which was also canceled.</cite>

<cite index="33-8">Musicians had criticized opera management over raises they said were given to executives, alleging that the orchestra's salary had only increased 16% from 2022 through 2025, while executive compensation for that same period ranged from an increase of 28% to 83%.</cite> <cite index="91-7">SF Opera had countered by underscoring the challenges of operating with a looming structural deficit of $15 million despite robust ticket sales and donations.</cite>

<cite index="30-5">General Director Matthew Shilvock thanked both negotiating committees and praised the involvement of Mayor Daniel Lurie, Matthew Goudeau, and the mediators for their work over the past week in reaching an agreement that addresses structural change while treating the musicians fairly.</cite> <cite index="34-7">Orchestra negotiating committee chair Gabe Young said the deal gives musicians a fair contract and stability, and thanked the public and Opera patrons "for their patience and support through what has been a challenging process."</cite>

topStories.headline: Supervisors Approve Trimmed OpenGov Contract — $28 Million Through 2029, Not the $38.9M Lurie Sought
topStories.dek: The Board voted 10-1 on Sept. 15 to extend the controversial PermitSF contract, shaving a decade off Mayor Lurie's original ask after questions arose over the software's performance.
topStories.body:
<cite index="39-7">In a 10-1 vote, the Board of Supervisors approved a contract extension of up to $28 million for OpenGov, the software that powers "PermitSF," Mayor Lurie's project that promises to be a one-stop shop for residents and businesses seeking permits.</cite> <cite index="39-8">The extension — of a contract that began in October through an initial no-bid, $5.9 million, one-year agreement — will last through 2029.</cite>

The vote resolved weeks of public debate at City Hall. <cite index="37-8,37-9">Almost a year ago, Mayor Daniel Lurie's office had awarded a $5.9 million contract for an ambitious overhaul of the city's permitting system to OpenGov, a largely untested tech firm with connections to his former nonprofit, Tipping Point — and without a formal bidding process, and over the objections of departmental staff.</cite> <cite index="42-3,42-4,42-5">Questions about how OpenGov was selected surfaced in October, when the SF Standard reported that the mayor's office had chosen the company under unusual circumstances and that it had ties to Lurie's nonprofit and administration. A majority of city staff had preferred a cheaper company over OpenGov, which was picked through a no-bid contract; the mayor is a former investor in the company through a family trust.</cite>

<cite index="42-7,42-8">Ahead of the vote, the city's permit chief had said the new OpenGov system was "exceeding" its targets — but the city's own data showed building and fire permits taking longer than before.</cite> <cite index="39-6">Lawmakers nonetheless advanced Mayor Lurie's initiative to simplify the city's onerous permitting process, effectively putting to rest nearly a year of controversy involving the vendor chosen for the effort.</cite>

<cite index="39-3">Mayor Lurie said the OpenGov extension "will help us build on this progress and deliver even better results for San Franciscans."</cite> Supervisor Jackie Fielder cast the sole dissenting vote. The Board also noted that the city's newly created inspector general is expected to release a separate report on how OpenGov was initially procured sometime this fall.

topStories.headline: Displaced by Fire, Tenderloin Museum Holds Annual Gala at War Memorial — and Races to Fund Expansion
topStories.dek: The museum's 11th annual fundraiser moves to the War Memorial Green Room on Sept. 23 after a June hotel fire above its Eddy Street home forced a temporary closure.
topStories.body:
<cite index="101-17,101-18">A fire on June 27 forced the Tenderloin Museum to close, the museum reported in an Instagram post. The fire originated "in the residential floors of The Cadillac Hotel, above our space."</cite> The museum has been holding programs at off-site venues ever since, including its regular Dodge Alley concerts and events at the Compton's Cafeteria Riot space on Larkin Street.

<cite index="103-1,103-2">The museum's 11th Annual Gala, "A Decade Plus One," is scheduled for Wednesday, September 23, from 5 to 8:30 p.m. at The Green Room at San Francisco War Memorial, 401 Van Ness Ave. Set against the backdrop of one of the city's most striking architectural settings, the night will bring together supporters for live entertainment, community voices, and distinctive food and drink.</cite>

<cite index="102-16,102-17">Eleven years ago, the Tenderloin Museum opened its doors in one of San Francisco's most misunderstood neighborhoods with a simple but radical idea: that the Tenderloin's stories deserved to be told with dignity, depth, and pride. Over the last decade, the museum has grown into a living, breathing cultural institution that is reshaping how this city sees itself.</cite>

<cite index="80-2,80-3">In 2026, the museum aims to open a new 6,850-square-foot space that triples its size, with a goal of raising $50,000 by December 31</cite> to complete the final phase of that fundraising campaign. <cite index="78-3">The museum's current gallery show, "Indigenous Forever," is on view through October 3, 2026.</cite> Tickets for the gala are available via Humanitix.

events.title: SF Symphony: Garrick Ohlsson Plays Brahms
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave
events.description: <cite index="110-1,110-2,110-3">Conductor David Afkham leads the orchestra in Unsuk Chin's subito con forza and Robert Schumann's Symphony No. 4, with internationally acclaimed pianist Garrick Ohlsson joining for Brahms' Piano Concerto No. 1.</cite> Inside Music Talks precede both performances.

events.title: "Valley of the Queens": Monthly LGBTQ+ History Walking Tour
events.location: Meets at SW corner of Geary and Powell St., Union Square
events.description: <cite index="77-4,77-5,77-6">The Tenderloin Museum partners with Unspeakable Vice for this monthly walking tour focused on LGBTQIA+ history in the Tenderloin and Polk Street neighborhoods. Created by CCA professor Shawn Sprockett, the tour traces queer belonging and history from the city's earliest days.</cite> Registration required via Humanitix.

events.title: SF Opera: Simon Boccanegra — Season Resumes
events.location: War Memorial Opera House, 301 Van Ness Ave
events.description: <cite index="83-5,83-6">San Francisco Opera's 2026–27 season finally opens with Music Director Eun Sun Kim leading an international cast in Giuseppe Verdi's Simon Boccanegra, presented in Claus Guth's production from the Hamburg State Opera.</cite> <cite index="84-7">A post-performance talkback with Music Director Eun Sun Kim follows the Sunday, September 27 matinee.</cite>

events.title: Tenderloin Museum 11th Annual Gala: "A Decade Plus One"
events.location: The Green Room, San Francisco War Memorial, 401 Van Ness Ave
events.description: <cite index="102-15">Tenderloin Museum's 11th Annual Gala brings together devoted supporters for a night of live entertainment, community voices, and distinctive food and drink, set against one of San Francisco's most stunning architectural backdrops.</cite> Tickets available via Humanitix; proceeds support the museum's ongoing expansion.

events.title: Fantastic Negrito with the SF Symphony
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave
events.description: <cite index="51-1">The San Francisco Symphony presents a special one-night performance featuring Grammy-winning Oakland artist Fantastic Negrito alongside the full orchestra.</cite> Part of the Symphony's 2026–27 season opener month.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack — Free Lunchtime Concerts
events.location: Fulton Plaza, 147 Fulton St (between Main Library and Asian Art Museum)
events.description: <cite index="92-3,92-4">The Civic Center Soundtrack has returned for its third season, with free live local music and food trucks every Tuesday and Thursday through October.</cite> The series is produced by Illuminate and presented in partnership with SF Rec and Park.

events.title: Fall Family Festival at Civic Center
events.description: <cite index="12-14">Taking place under the twinkling Spectra lights, the Fall Family Festival features fun carnival games, free pumpkin decorating, face painting, the San Francisco Public Library Bookmobile, and entertainment including stilt walkers and bubble magic.</cite> Free and open to all ages.

moreNews.headline: Live on Larkin Free Street Festival Continues Every Second Saturday Through December
moreNews.body: <cite index="121-10,121-11,121-12">Live on Larkin — a series of free street events on Larkin Street between Ellis and Eddy — runs every second Saturday from noon to 5 p.m. through December 2026, with live music, performances, free activities, games, and vendors.</cite> The series is funded in part by crypto entrepreneur Chris Larsen's $5 million donation to the Tenderloin Community Benefit District and is part of a broader effort to activate the Larkin Street corridor.

moreNews.headline: Tenderloin Museum Gallery: "Indigenous Forever" Open Through October 3
moreNews.body: <cite index="78-3,78-4">"Indigenous Forever," a gallery show of paintings by Adrian Arias honoring the strength and continuity of Indigenous cultures, is on view at the Tenderloin Museum through October 3, 2026, and is free to attend with no registration required.</cite> <cite index="78-1,78-2">Tenderloin regulars may recognize imagery from the show — many of the paintings served as studies for an evocative mural of the same name unveiled on Larkin Street in spring 2025.</cite>

restaurants.name: Brenda's French Soul Food
restaurants.description: A beloved Tenderloin institution famed for beignets, shrimp and grits, and a weekday lineup of $5 breakfast sandwiches with New Orleans flair.

restaurants.name: Saigon Sandwich
restaurants.description: A Tenderloin institution since the early 1980s serving fresh, affordable bánh mì that The New York Times Magazine once called the best in the country.

restaurants.name: Outta Sight Pizza
restaurants.description: Popular Tenderloin slice shop serving excellent thin-crust pizza by the slice in an unpretentious neighborhood setting on Larkin Street.

restaurants.name: Mensho Tokyo
restaurants.description: Michelin-recognized ramen bar famed for its Toripaitan and Duck Matcha ramen, drawing devoted lines since opening its first U.S. location in the Tenderloin in 2016.

restaurants.name: Pho 2000
restaurants.description: Casual Little Saigon spot in the Tenderloin serving authentic phở, vermicelli bowls, and Vietnamese classics at very reasonable prices.

restaurants.name: Chao Pescao
restaurants.description: Vibrant Tenderloin spot serving Latin American cuisine including tostones, seafood dishes, and creative cocktails in a lively atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen
restaurants.description: Welcoming Tenderloin restaurant serving traditional Ethiopian stews, injera, and generous vegetarian platters in a warm communal setting.

restaurants.name: Wanjai Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: Family-run Tenderloin restaurant serving Northern Thai cuisine including khao soi, grilled meats, and house specialty noodles in an inviting atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Ararat Kebab & Gyros
restaurants.description: Tenderloin counter-service spot renowned for its kofte, gyros, and Turkish-style kebabs; a consistent neighborhood favorite.

restaurants.name: Azalina's
restaurants.description: A Tenderloin gem offering beautifully crafted Malaysian street food elevated with California ingredients in a stunning, art-filled dining room.

restaurants.name: Sungho
restaurants.description: A fantastic Korean comfort food spot in the Tenderloin drawing neighborhood regulars and cross-city visitors for warming, hearty dishes.

restaurants.name: Hai Ky Noodles
restaurants.description: A beloved Tenderloin noodle shop in Little Saigon specializing in egg noodles, wonton soup, and strong Vietnamese iced coffee.

restaurants.name: Villon
restaurants.description: All-day restaurant inside the San Francisco Proper Hotel serving seasonal California cuisine in a Kelly Wearstler-designed space with artistic flair.

restaurants.name: Charmaine's
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's most sought-after rooftop bars, atop the SF Proper Hotel, with panoramic city skyline views, craft cocktails, and a fire pit.
restaurants.address: 45 McAllister St, rooftop, San Francisco, CA 94102

restaurants.name: Bodega SF
restaurants.description: A laid-back Tenderloin bar and kitchen offering hearty comfort food and a well-stocked bar in a relaxed neighborhood setting.

hotels.name: San Francisco Proper Hotel
hotels.description: A 131-room luxury hotel inside a historic 1904 Beaux-Arts flatiron building on Market Street, with Kelly Wearstler interiors, a rooftop bar, and four dining venues.
hotels.address: 45 McAllister St (entrance; 1100 Market St), San Francisco, CA 94102

hotels.name: Phoenix Hotel
hotels.description: Iconic rock-and-roll motor lodge open under new ownership since early 2026, with a courtyard pool, free parking, and nearly 40 years of musical legend.

hotels.name: The Tilden Hotel
hotels.description: A stylish boutique hotel near Union Square and Civic Center with a relaxed atmosphere and a well-regarded breakfast, convenient for arts and theater visits.

hotels.name: Civic Center Motor Inn
hotels.description: A budget-friendly, centrally located motel in Mid-Market within walking distance of Davies Symphony Hall, the War Memorial Opera House, and Civic Center BART.

hotels.name: Motel 6 San Francisco – Civic Center
hotels.description: No-frills economy motel five minutes on foot from the Asian Art Museum and convenient to BART and Muni at Civic Center.

hotels.name: Hotel Epik San Francisco
hotels.description: A four-star hotel with modern amenities and meeting space, situated ten minutes on foot from Civic Center/UN Plaza with easy BART and Muni access.
hotels.address: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102

shops.name: Heart of the City Farmers Market
shops.description: A year-round outdoor farmers market at United Nations Plaza offering fresh produce, specialty foods, and prepared items from Bay Area growers, held Wednesday and Sunday mornings.
shops.address: United Nations Plaza, Fulton St at Market St, Civic Center

shops.name: Asian Art Museum Store
shops.description: Boutique inside the Asian Art Museum stocking one-of-a-kind objects, jewelry, books, and gifts sourced from across Asia; no paid museum admission required to browse.

shops.name: SF Main Library Wednesday Used Book Sale
shops.description: Every Wednesday, the Larkin Street steps of the SF Main Library host a browseable used book sale spanning all genres; free and open to all.

shops.name: Artisan Gift Gallery at Fulton Plaza
shops.description: An ongoing artisan gift gallery at Fulton Plaza selling handcrafted goods from local makers as part of the Civic Center public space activation program.

shops.name: Onsen SF
shops.description: A Japanese-inspired bathhouse in the Tenderloin offering communal mineral soaking baths, private rooms, and rotating dinner pop-ups in an intimate setting.

artEntertainment.name: Asian Art Museum
artEntertainment.description: One of the largest museums dedicated to Asian art in the Western world, housing more than 18,000 works spanning 6,000 years of history in a landmark Civic Center building.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Main Public Library
artEntertainment.description: The seven-story Main Branch of the SF Public Library serves as a vibrant cultural hub at Civic Center, hosting exhibitions, lectures, film screenings, and community events year-round.

artEntertainment.name: War Memorial Opera House
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's grand opera house, home to the San Francisco Opera and San Francisco Ballet, in a landmark Beaux-Arts building at the heart of the Civic Center arts campus.
artEntertainment.address: 301 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102

artEntertainment.name: Davies Symphony Hall
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Symphony since 1980, this landmark Civic Center hall hosts the Symphony's full season plus touring orchestras and special events.
artEntertainment.address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.description: The first free-standing building in America built specifically for jazz performance and education, presenting over 300 shows annually at the corner of Franklin and Fell Streets.

artEntertainment.name: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium
artEntertainment.description: An 8,500-capacity landmark arena built in 1915, operated by Another Planet Entertainment and hosting more than 100 concerts and events per year on the Civic Center campus.

artEntertainment.name: The Warfield Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A 2,250-capacity Mid-Market concert hall opened in 1922 as a vaudeville palace, now operated by Goldenvoice and hosting major touring acts year-round.

artEntertainment.name: Great American Music Hall
artEntertainment.description: A storied Tenderloin music hall with ornate Baroque décor, hosting an eclectic mix of rock, jazz, folk, and roots artists throughout the year since 1972.

artEntertainment.name: The Tenderloin Museum
artEntertainment.description: A museum and walking-tour program dedicated to the history, culture, and resilience of the Tenderloin; currently closed for flood repairs while fundraising to reopen and expand.

artEntertainment.name: Rickshaw Stop
artEntertainment.description: A beloved mid-sized venue near Civic Center hosting indie rock, electronic, dance nights, and DJ events in a comfortable two-room space.

gymsRecreation.name: United Nations Plaza Fitness Court
gymsRecreation.description: A free outdoor Fitness Court by the National Fitness Campaign at United Nations Plaza, offering strength-training equipment and free group exercise classes through Rae Studios.

gymsRecreation.name: UN Plaza Skateboarding Area
gymsRecreation.description: A 13,000-square-foot skateboarding zone at United Nations Plaza featuring iconic elements from San Francisco's street skating history, open to all skill levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Civic Center Plaza Free Yoga and Zumba
gymsRecreation.description: Free Zumba and yoga classes held regularly at Civic Center Plaza and United Nations Plaza, part of the Rec and Park and Civic Center Community Benefit District activation program.
gymsRecreation.address: Civic Center Plaza, Van Ness Ave & Grove St, Civic Center

gymsRecreation.name: Fulton Plaza Open Roller Skating
gymsRecreation.description: All-ages open roller skating at Fulton Plaza between the Main Library and the Asian Art Museum; bring your own skates or blades.

gymsRecreation.name: Tenderloin Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: A city-run recreation center in the Tenderloin offering gym facilities, youth sports programming, and community classes in one of the neighborhood's few safe recreational spaces.

gymsRecreation.name: Boeddeker Park
gymsRecreation.description: A fully renovated Tenderloin park at Eddy and Jones Streets with a playground, basketball court, and green space serving as one of the neighborhood's primary outdoor gathering spots.

gymsRecreation.name: Onsen SF
gymsRecreation.description: A serene Japanese-inspired bathhouse in the Tenderloin offering communal mineral baths and private soaking rooms.

gymsRecreation.name: SVN West
gymsRecreation.type: Multi-use event venue with recreational programming
gymsRecreation.description: A large Mid-Market event space that periodically hosts a rooftop Sky Rink skating experience and fitness pop-ups alongside concerts and private events.
